text_note.zh: 这里用的是《唐诗三百首》等书里通行的文字。数据库原文有几处不同：第五句首字是“摐”的异体字，“旌旆”原作“旌旗”；第十句“凭陵”原作“凭凌”；第十三句“腓”原作“衰”；第十四句“斗”原作“鬬”（繁体）；第二十一句“边庭飘飖”原作“边风飘飘”；第二十二句“无所有”原作“更何有”；第二十三句“三时”原作“三日”。这些多是不同版本的写法。原诗前面还有一段序，这里没有收入正文。
text_note.en: This is the text found in Three Hundred Tang Poems and most common editions. The corpus differs in several places. Line 5 begins with a variant form of chuāng, and has jīng qí (banners) for jīng pèi (flags). Line 10 has a variant character for líng. Line 13 has shuāi (wither) for féi (wilt). Line 14 has the traditional form of dòu (fight). Line 21 has biān fēng piāo piāo (the border wind blows) for biān tíng piāo yáo (the border lands are wild and far). Line 22 has gèng hé yǒu (what else is there) for wú suǒ yǒu (there is nothing). Line 23 has sān rì (three days) for sān shí (all day). These are mostly differences between old editions. The poem also has a short preface, which is not part of the lines here.

readings.zh: 汉将：汉朝的将领，“将”读 jiàng。
readings.en: In hàn jiàng, “the Han general”, this character means general and is read jiàng.

readings.zh: 横行：在战场上纵横冲杀，读 héng xíng。
readings.en: In héng xíng, “charging freely across the field”, this character is read héng.
This character means to strike and is read chuāng.

readings.zh: 校尉：一种武官，“校”读 xiào，不读 jiào。
readings.en: In xiào wèi, an army officer, this character is read xiào, not jiào.

readings.zh: 单于：匈奴首领的称号，读 chán yú，不读 dān。
readings.en: In chán yú, the title of the Xiongnu ruler, this character is read chán, not dān.

readings.zh: 塞草：边塞上的草，“塞”读 sài。
readings.en: In sài cǎo, “border grass”, this character is read sài.

readings.zh: 少妇：年轻的妻子，“少”读 shào。
readings.en: In shào fù, “young wife”, this character is read shào.

readings.zh: 那可度：哪里能越过。“那”同“哪”，现在一般读 nǎ，也有书读 nuó。
readings.en: In nǎ kě dù, “how can one cross”, this character means “how” and is usually read nǎ; some books read it nuó.

readings.zh: 刁斗：军中的铜锅，读 diāo dǒu，不读 dòu。
readings.en: In diāo dǒu, an army bronze pot, this character is read dǒu, not dòu.

glosses.zh: 汉家：汉朝，这里借指唐朝。唐代诗人常用汉朝来说本朝的事。
glosses.en: hàn jiā: the Han dynasty, standing for the Tang. Tang poets often wrote of their own times as “Han”.

glosses.zh: 烟尘：烽火的烟和战马扬起的尘土，指战争。
glosses.en: yān chén: the smoke of beacon fires and the dust of horses, meaning war.

glosses.zh: 破残贼：打败凶残的敌人。
glosses.en: pò cán zéi: to crush the cruel enemy.

glosses.zh: 本自：本来就。
glosses.en: běn zì: by nature, already.

glosses.zh: 重横行：看重在战场上纵横冲杀、所向无敌。
glosses.en: zhòng héng xíng: to prize charging freely across the battlefield, beaten by no one.

glosses.zh: 非常赐颜色：格外给他们好脸色，特别器重和奖赏他们。
glosses.en: fēi cháng cì yán sè: showing them unusual favor and rewards.

glosses.zh: 摐金伐鼓：敲着锣，打着鼓。金，锣一类的铜乐器；伐，敲击。
glosses.en: chuāng jīn fá gǔ: striking gongs and beating drums. Jīn is a bronze gong; fá means to beat.

glosses.zh: 下榆关：开出榆关。榆关就是山海关，在今天河北秦皇岛。
glosses.en: xià yú guān: marching out through Yu Pass, today's Shanhai Pass near Qinhuangdao in Hebei.

glosses.zh: 旌旆：各种各样的军旗。
glosses.en: jīng pèi: all kinds of army flags.

glosses.zh: 逶迤：弯弯曲曲、连绵不断的样子。
glosses.en: wēi yí: winding on and on.

glosses.zh: 碣石：山名，在今天河北昌黎附近的海边。
glosses.en: jié shí: Jieshi Mountain, by the sea near today's Changli in Hebei.

glosses.zh: 校尉：比将军低一级的武官。
glosses.en: xiào wèi: an army officer, one rank below a general.

glosses.zh: 羽书：插着羽毛的紧急军事文书。
glosses.en: yǔ shū: an urgent army message with feathers stuck on it.

glosses.zh: 瀚海：大沙漠。
glosses.en: hàn hǎi: the great desert.

glosses.zh: 单于：匈奴首领的称号，这里指敌人的首领。
glosses.en: chán yú: the title of the Xiongnu ruler, here the enemy chief.

glosses.zh: 猎火：打猎时点起的火。古代北方民族常借打猎来演练军队，所以这是要来进攻的信号。
glosses.en: liè huǒ: hunting fires. Northern peoples often trained for war by hunting, so the fires warn of an attack.

glosses.zh: 狼山：狼居胥山，在今天内蒙古一带，这里泛指边境的山。
glosses.en: láng shān: Wolf Mountain, in today's Inner Mongolia, here any mountain on the border.

glosses.zh: 萧条：冷落荒凉。
glosses.en: xiāo tiáo: bleak and empty.

glosses.zh: 极边土：一直到边境的尽头。极，尽头。
glosses.en: jí biān tǔ: all the way to the farthest edge of the border. Jí means the very end.

glosses.zh: 胡骑：敌人的骑兵。
glosses.en: hú qí: enemy horsemen.

glosses.zh: 凭陵：仗着势力欺压，横冲直撞。
glosses.en: píng líng: trampling over others by force.

glosses.zh: 杂风雨：像夹着狂风暴雨一样冲来。
glosses.en: zá fēng yǔ: rushing in like wind and rain.

glosses.zh: 半死生：一半人战死，一半人还活着，指死伤很多。
glosses.en: bàn sǐ shēng: half dead, half alive, meaning very many killed.

glosses.zh: 帐下：将军的营帐里。
glosses.en: zhàng xià: in the general's tent.

glosses.zh: 犹歌舞：还在唱歌跳舞取乐。
glosses.en: yóu gē wǔ: still singing and dancing for fun.

glosses.zh: 穷秋：深秋，秋天快完的时候。
glosses.en: qióng qiū: late autumn, the very end of autumn.

glosses.zh: 腓：草木枯萎、变黄。
glosses.en: féi: to wilt and turn yellow.

glosses.zh: 斗兵稀：能打仗的士兵越来越少了。
glosses.en: dòu bīng xī: fewer and fewer soldiers left to fight.

glosses.zh: 身当恩遇：自己受到皇上的恩宠。这里指将领。
glosses.en: shēn dāng ēn yù: having received the emperor's favor. This means the general.

glosses.zh: 轻敌：看不起敌人，不把敌人放在眼里。
glosses.en: qīng dí: taking the enemy too lightly.

glosses.zh: 关山：关口和山岭，指边塞。
glosses.en: guān shān: passes and mountains, meaning the frontier.

glosses.zh: 未解围：还没能冲破敌人的包围。
glosses.en: wèi jiě wéi: still unable to break the siege.

glosses.zh: 铁衣：铁甲，这里指穿铁甲的士兵。
glosses.en: tiě yī: iron armor, here the soldiers who wear it.

glosses.zh: 远戍：到远方去守边。戍，守卫边疆。
glosses.en: yuǎn shù: guarding a faraway border. Shù means to guard the frontier.

glosses.zh: 玉箸：玉做的筷子，比喻妻子流下的两行眼泪。箸，筷子。
glosses.en: yù zhù: jade chopsticks, a picture of the two lines of tears on a wife's face. Zhù means chopsticks.

glosses.zh: 应啼：想必一直在哭。应，想来、应该。
glosses.en: yīng tí: must surely be weeping. Yīng means surely, no doubt.

glosses.zh: 城南：指家乡的城南，妻子住的地方。
glosses.en: chéng nán: the south of the home town, where the wife lives.

glosses.zh: 欲断肠：伤心得肠子都要断了，形容极度悲伤。
glosses.en: yù duàn cháng: so sad her heart might break.

glosses.zh: 征人：出征的士兵。
glosses.en: zhēng rén: a soldier sent to war.

glosses.zh: 蓟北：蓟州以北，在今天天津、河北北部一带，这里指边地。
glosses.en: jì běi: north of Jizhou, around today's Tianjin and northern Hebei, here the frontier.

glosses.zh: 空回首：白白地回头望着家乡，却回不去。
glosses.en: kōng huí shǒu: looking back toward home in vain.

glosses.zh: 边庭：边疆。
glosses.en: biān tíng: the border lands.

glosses.zh: 飘飖：动荡不安、遥远的样子。
glosses.en: piāo yáo: wild, unsettled and far away.

glosses.zh: 那可度：哪里能越过、哪里能回去。
glosses.en: nǎ kě dù: how could one cross it and go home.

glosses.zh: 绝域：极远的地方。
glosses.en: jué yù: a land at the end of the earth.

glosses.zh: 无所有：什么也没有，一片荒凉。
glosses.en: wú suǒ yǒu: nothing at all, only emptiness.

glosses.zh: 杀气：战场上阴森可怕的气氛。
glosses.en: shā qì: the grim air of killing on a battlefield.

glosses.zh: 三时：早、中、晚，指一整天。
glosses.en: sān shí: morning, noon and evening, meaning all day.

glosses.zh: 阵云：像军阵一样的浓云，古人认为是打仗的征兆。
glosses.en: zhèn yún: heavy clouds shaped like battle lines, thought to be a sign of war.

glosses.zh: 寒声：凄冷的声音。
glosses.en: hán shēng: a cold, bleak sound.

glosses.zh: 刁斗：军中用的铜锅，白天用来做饭，夜里敲着它报时、巡夜。
glosses.en: diāo dǒu: an army bronze pot, used for cooking by day and struck at night to mark the hours.

glosses.zh: 白刃：雪亮的刀。
glosses.en: bái rèn: a gleaming blade.

glosses.zh: 死节：为了国家献出生命，守住气节。
glosses.en: sǐ jié: dying for one's country, keeping faith to the end.

glosses.zh: 岂顾勋：哪里是为了个人的功劳。顾，顾及；勋，功劳。
glosses.en: qǐ gù xūn: not for personal glory. Gù means to care about; xūn means honors.

glosses.zh: 沙场：战场。
glosses.en: shā chǎng: the battlefield.

glosses.zh: 李将军：一般认为指汉朝名将李广。他爱护士兵，匈奴很怕他。一说指战国时赵国名将李牧。
glosses.en: lǐ jiāng jūn: usually taken to be Li Guang, a famous Han general who cared for his men and was feared by the Xiongnu. Another reading says it is Li Mu, a great general of the state of Zhao.

translation.zh: 国家的东北边境燃起了战火，
translation.en: War smoke rises on the empire's northeast border;

translation.zh: 将军们告别家人，出征去打败凶残的敌人。
translation.en: the generals leave their homes to crush the cruel enemy.

translation.zh: 男子汉本来就看重在战场上纵横冲杀，
translation.en: Brave men by nature prize charging across the battlefield;

translation.zh: 何况皇上又格外器重和奖赏他们。
translation.en: and the emperor shows them special favor.

translation.zh: 敲锣打鼓，大军开出了榆关，
translation.en: With gongs and drums the army marches out through Yu Pass;

translation.zh: 军旗弯弯曲曲，连绵在碣石山一带。
translation.en: its flags wind on and on around Jieshi Mountain.

translation.zh: 校尉的紧急军书飞快地传过大沙漠，
translation.en: An officer's urgent message flies across the great desert:

translation.zh: 敌人首领打猎的火光照亮了狼山。
translation.en: the enemy chief's hunting fires light up Wolf Mountain.

translation.zh: 山河荒凉冷落，一直延伸到边境尽头，
translation.en: Hills and rivers lie bleak to the farthest edge of the border;

translation.zh: 敌人的骑兵横冲直撞，像狂风暴雨一样扑来。
translation.en: enemy horsemen charge in like wind and rain.

translation.zh: 战士们在阵前拼杀，死伤了一大半，
translation.en: At the front, half the soldiers die and half live on;

translation.zh: 将军的营帐里，美人还在唱歌跳舞。
translation.en: in the general's tent, beautiful women still sing and dance.

translation.zh: 深秋的大沙漠里，边塞的草都枯黄了，
translation.en: In the great desert at autumn's end, the border grass has withered;

translation.zh: 夕阳下的孤城中，能打仗的士兵越来越少。
translation.en: in the lonely fort at sunset, few soldiers are left to fight.

translation.zh: 将军受了皇恩，常常看不起敌人，
translation.en: The general, proud of the emperor's favor, takes the enemy lightly;

translation.zh: 士兵们在关山拼尽了力气，还是冲不出包围。
translation.en: the soldiers spend all their strength in the passes and still cannot break the siege.

translation.zh: 穿着铁甲守卫远方的边疆，辛苦了很久很久，
translation.en: In iron armor they guard the faraway border, through long, hard years;

translation.zh: 自从分别以后，家中的妻子想必一直在流泪。
translation.en: since they parted, their wives at home must have wept and wept.

translation.zh: 城南的少妇伤心得肝肠欲断，
translation.en: In the south of the town, a young wife is broken with grief;

translation.zh: 蓟北的战士白白地回头遥望家乡。
translation.en: north of Ji, her soldier husband looks back toward home in vain.

translation.zh: 边疆动荡遥远，哪里能越过回家？
translation.en: The border lands are wild and far; how can he cross them?

translation.zh: 极远的边地一片苍茫，什么也没有。
translation.en: The land at the earth's end is vast and dim, with nothing in it.

translation.zh: 一整天杀气腾腾，浓云像军阵一样压着；
translation.en: All day the air of killing hangs in clouds like battle lines;

translation.zh: 整整一夜，只听见凄冷的刁斗声。
translation.en: all night the cold sound of the watch pot rings out.

translation.zh: 战士们互相看着雪亮的刀上鲜血淋淋，
translation.en: The men look at one another's blades, wet with blood;

translation.zh: 为国而死，从来就不是为了个人的功劳。
translation.en: those who die for their country have never done it for glory.

translation.zh: 你没看见战场上打仗有多么苦吗？
translation.en: Do you not see how bitter it is to fight on the battlefield?

translation.zh: 直到今天，人们还在怀念爱护士兵的李将军。
translation.en: Even now people still long for General Li, who cared for his men.

background.zh: 这首诗前面有一段序，大意是：开元二十六年（738年），有人跟随御史大夫张公（一般认为是幽州节度使张守珪）出塞回来，写了一首《燕歌行》给高适看。高适有感于边塞打仗守边的事，就和了这首。“燕歌行”是乐府旧题，燕指今天河北北部一带，古代多写边塞征战和离别相思。一说诗中暗讽张守珪手下将领打了败仗却隐瞒不报。
background.en: The poem has a short preface. It says that in 738 a man who had gone out to the border with a high official named Zhang (usually taken to be Zhang Shougui, the military governor of Youzhou) came back and showed Gao Shi a poem called “Song of Yan”. Moved by the hard life of soldiers on the frontier, Gao Shi wrote this poem in reply. “Song of Yan” is an old yuefu title. Yan is the land of today's northern Hebei, and songs under this title were about war on the border and missing loved ones. Some readers think the poem quietly criticizes Zhang Shougui's officers, who lost a battle and hid it.

author_note.zh: 高适（约704—765），字达夫，唐代著名诗人。他年轻时生活贫困，曾多次到北方边塞游历，亲眼见过守边将士的生活。后来他做官做到节度使，是唐代诗人里官位最高的之一。他和岑参都擅长写边塞诗，合称“高岑”。《燕歌行》被认为是他最好的作品。
author_note.en: Gao Shi (about 704–765), also called Dafu, was a famous Tang poet. He was poor when young and travelled several times to the northern frontier, where he saw the soldiers' life with his own eyes. Later he rose to be a military governor, one of the highest posts any Tang poet held. He and Cen Shen were both masters of frontier poems and are named together as Gao and Cen. This poem is thought to be his finest work.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一部战争长卷。开头是出征的热闹：锣鼓喧天，旌旗飘扬，皇上赏识，人人想立功。接着气氛一下子变紧：军书飞驰，敌人的火光照亮山头，骑兵像暴风雨一样扑来。最扎心的是两句对照：阵前的士兵死伤一半，营帐里的美人还在唱歌跳舞。然后镜头转到秋天的孤城，士兵越来越少，又转到千里外流泪的妻子和回头望家的丈夫。最后是血光闪闪的刀和士兵们不求功名的决心。结尾一句怀念李将军，说出了士兵们最大的心愿：希望有一位真正爱护他们的将军。诗里有豪情，也有愤怒和同情。
appreciation.en: The poem is like a long war painting. It opens with the noise of marching out: gongs and drums, waving flags, the emperor's favor, everyone eager for glory. Then the mood tightens. Messages race, enemy fires light the hills, horsemen sweep in like a storm. The sharpest moment is a pair of lines side by side: half the soldiers at the front are killed, while in the general's tent women still sing and dance. Then we see the lonely fort in autumn with fewer and fewer men, and a wife weeping a thousand miles away while her husband looks back toward home. At the end come blood-wet blades and soldiers who fight not for glory. The last line, longing for General Li, speaks their deepest wish: a general who truly cares for them. The poem holds courage, anger and pity all at once.
